openItems.explanation: The June 30, 2026 accrued wages, $314,193.69, are cut off correctly, but the employer’s Social Security and Medicare on them, $22,864.35 at the July 10 payroll’s own rate, was expensed when paid and never accrued (Q6). The same was true at June 30, 2025 ($19,972.25), so FY2026 expense is understated $2,892.10 and liabilities $22,864.35. Proposed: debit 6210 $2,892.10 and partners’ capital $19,972.25 (the prior year’s, if the CPA treats it so), credit 2210 $22,864.35. Over clearly trivial, under performance materiality: passed if the client declines. Paid Leave and L&I employer premiums on the accrual are smaller and not estimated. The machine never posts.

Renata Salazar, Payroll and HR Manager, entered her own increase from $88,000.00 to $98,000.00 effective December 22, 2025, and its personnel action form PAF-25-119 is not signed. Q4 says the Managing Director agreed it in her review. $4,999.93 more was paid in 13 paychecks to June 30. The pay is recorded correctly; the question is authorization. Ask the Managing Director to confirm and sign the form, and the CPA weighs it as a control deficiency: the person who keeps the master file can change her own pay.

The payroll system takes the L&I employee share on time and a half for each overtime hour (Q7); L&I counts an overtime hour as one hour and an employer may not deduct more than the share. The sample shows $4.94 over-deducted on 3 paychecks; at the year’s 8,570 overtime hours it is roughly $2,514.64, owed back to the crews, and the setup is still wrong in the Q3 2026 payrolls. A person fixes the setup and arranges the refunds.

Xavier Baptiste (E-1044) and Alicia Baptiste (E-1051) are paid into the same account. Cleared by inquiry (Q3) and the personnel files: they are married, each has an I-9, a W-4 and a signed deposit form naming the joint account, and their hours are approved by different superintendents. No further work is proposed; the CPA reviews the clearance.
Materiality is proposed at $350,000.00, 12100000.0% of the year’s revenue, with performance materiality $262,500.00 and clearly trivial $17,500.00. The engagement partner sets the final amounts.
No management representation letter has been obtained. The CPA requests it near the end of fieldwork, covering the payroll answers relied on here.
These are draft workpapers and findings for the engagement partner. They are not an audit report and give no opinion. Nothing has been signed, posted or sent to the client.
